input: It is recommended that a metered trial of the heat-recovery retrofit be carried out on one of the three refrigeration lines before any capital decision is taken, and the plant engineer will own the trial. To provide some context, refrigeration at the food plant currently uses some 2443 MWh of electricity per year, and the case for the retrofit rests essentially on a projection provided by the equipment vendor rather than on anything that has been measured at the plant itself. According to the vendor, the retrofit is projected to save 13% of that electricity use, which corresponds to a derived saving of 318 MWh per year at the vendor figure. At an electricity price of $0.13 per kWh, this works out to a derived annual saving of $41k, which can be set against a capital cost of $428k to give a derived simple payback of 10.4 years. It is important to emphasise that the saving figure has not been measured at this plant, and that refrigeration load in the summer peak month was not modelled, so the payback should really be read as a figure that holds at the vendor projection and outside the peak month. A metered trial on a single line would replace the projection with a measured saving for that line, and the capital decision could then be taken on the basis of the trial result together with a modelled peak month, which would represent a considerably firmer footing for a decision of this size.
target: A metered trial on one of the three refrigeration lines is recommended before any capital decision on the heat-recovery retrofit; the plant engineer owns the trial. Refrigeration at the food plant uses 2443 MWh of electricity per year, and the case for the retrofit rests on the equipment vendor's projection, not on measurement at the plant. The vendor projects a saving of 13% of the refrigeration use, a derived saving of 318 MWh per year at the vendor figure. At an electricity price of $0.13 per kWh, the derived annual saving is $41k against a capital cost of $428k, and the derived simple payback is 10.4 years. The saving figure was not measured at this plant, and refrigeration load in the summer peak month was not modelled; the payback holds at the vendor figure and outside the peak month. The trial is metered, so the saving on the trial line is measured at the loads the line actually carries, including its part-load operation. The capital decision then rests on evidence from this plant rather than on a projection made for a general case. The recommendation holds the capital decision open until the two gaps in the evidence, measurement at this plant and the peak month, are closed. The capital decision then rests on the trial result and on a modelled peak month, and a trial that fails to reproduce the projected saving ends the proposal at the cost of metering one line.
